About GiveDirectly In The DRC GiveDirectly DRC was established in 2018 to enable cash transfers to poor and rural populations via mobile phones, thereby promoting food security, poverty reduction, and financial inclusion. We aimed to demonstrate the operational feasibility and cost-effectiveness of transferring large volumes of money digitally in one of the world's least developed countries. Since its inception four years ago, GiveDirectly DRC has used mobile phones to transfer over $14 million to more than 65,000 beneficiaries in four provinces: South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, and Kinshasa. GiveDirectly's activities in the DRC have expanded to include, among other things: compelling proofs of concept for mobile-based cash transfers; and the implementation of innovative technologies to target disadvantaged urban populations in Kinshasa, in collaboration with the DRC's social protection agency, the DRC Social Fund. The delivery of contactless cash to beneficiaries in Beni and Bunia affected by the economic consequences of COVID-19. You will be joining Give Directly DRC at an exciting time in its history, as we are establishing and hope to launch several new programs and strengthen our partnership with the DRC government. About The Role As Senior Manager, Programs (DRC), you'll help bring GiveDirectly's programs in the Democratic Republic of Congo to life — owning their end-to-end execution, from operational design to on-the-ground delivery. You'll blend strategic thinking with hands-on problem-solving: designing systems that work, catching risks before they escalate, and using data to drive continuous improvement. You'll also lead people, managing a team of managers and field staff, while partnering closely with the Program Director and Country Director to shape what comes next. It's a role for someone who's energized by both the big picture and the operational details that make it real. What You’ll Do Develop detailed project management plans for all our programs and drive them through successful end-to-end execution Design operational models for new programs — including targeting, payments, and customer service — and define, monitor, and report on key operational and efficiency indicators Identify operational vulnerabilities, such as fraud or reputational risk, and implement mitigation solutions aligned with the risk framework set by the Program Director Analyze program-level data to diagnose the causes of underperformance and drive continuous quality improvement Partner with Tech and Data teams to design surveys and ensure data integrity in Salesforce Directly manage a team of managers, with oversight of field teams and call centre at multiple levels Support the Program Director and Country Director in scoping new programs, including operational feasibility and risk assessment. Manage partner relationships with key operational partners with oversight of scoping, contracting and ensuring the terms of our agreements are respected. Develop materials for engagement with donors and other external stakeholders in order to represent our work externally. Requirements Minimum 6 years of experience managing and implementing programs within international NGOs or a comparable operational environment; experience in cash or money transfer programming is an asset Work experience in the DRC, or strong knowledge of the DRC context, is highly desirable Experience in team management, including recruitment, team building, and development Strong analytical thinking, with a proven ability to use data to identify problems and improve programs Experience using technology and digital tools to drive results and operational innovation Proven instinct for risk management and creative problem-solving in complex operational environments A high degree of autonomy and resilience, with the ability to thrive in a fragile, rapidly changing environment Strong alignment with GiveDirectly's values Excellent written and oral communication skills, including ability to communicate fluently in English and French with high level stakeholders Professional proficiency in French and English required; knowledge of Congolese Swahili and/or Lingala is an asset Compensation At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here . Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income. Base Salary: $94,500 Bonus at Target Performance: 10% (~$9,450, with potential for upside. For reference, with the organization’s current performance multiplier, this amount would be $11,057 in 2025) Estimated Total Compensation at Target: $103,950+ This role is onsite in Goma, DRC. We welcome candidates based in the DRC as well as those willing to relocate to be based in the DRC. Working at GiveDirectly GiveDirectly is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to the person’s race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant. Commitment to Safeguarding As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. To that end, GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and will systematically check with previous employers about any abuse or misconduct related matters involving potential new hires. We may also employ other robust pre-hire screens, including in-depth reference checks, criminal background checks, and sanctions screens. If you require any accommodations during the application or interview process, or to perform the essential functions of the role, please email us at careers@givedirectly.org with the email subject “Accommodation Needed”. We will work with you to ensure reasonable accommodations are made to support your needs. Want to put your best foot forward on your GiveDirectly application? About About the Project Office En Tunisie, l’UNICEF appuie le Gouvernement dans le renforcement des systèmes et des politiques publiques visant à garantir les droits et le bien-être des enfants. Dans les domaines de la protection sociale et de la protection de l’enfance, l’organisation accompagne le Ministère des Affaires Sociales (MAS) dans le développement de systèmes plus inclusifs, efficaces et résilients, notamment à travers le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles, l’amélioration des mécanismes de coordination intersectoriels, le développement des systèmes d’information et la production d’évidences pour éclairer les politiques publiques. Dans le cadre de ce partenariat, l’UNICEF soutient le développement d’une approche intégrée du travail social (social services workforce integration) favorisant une meilleure articulation entre les systèmes de protection sociale et de protection de l’enfance afin d’assurer un continuum de services pour les enfants vulnérables et leurs familles. Cette approche vise à renforcer la coordination entre les acteurs, les mécanismes de référencement et les capacités des travailleurs sociaux et d’autres intervenants de première ligne des services à l’enfance pour améliorer l’accès à des services de qualité. Le/La Senior Integrated Social Services Associate apportera un appui technique et opérationnel à la mise en œuvre, au suivi et à la coordination des activités conjointes UNICEF–MAS. Les résultats de cette fonction soutiennent le renforcement des systèmes nationaux et favorisent la mise en place d’un continuum de services plus coordonné, inclusif et centré sur les besoins des enfants. Des missions sur le terrain en dehors de Tunis seront à prévoir, notamment afin d’accompagner la mise en œuvre et le suivi des activités sur le terrain. Elles seront pris en charge par l’UNICEF. Child Safeguarding Le/la titulaire du poste adhère aux politiques de l’UNICEF en matière de sauvegarde de l’enfant, de prévention de l’exploitation et des abus sexuels (PSEA) et de conduite éthique. Demonstrated comfort communicating effectively both internally and externally: on the team, as well as across Anduril’s many other business lines, software platforms, organizations and clients. Experience with complex problem solving, proactive planning, rehearsals and troubleshooting to ensure seamless, transparent customer experience. Successful teammates have demonstrated a level of ‘healthy paranoia’ that borders on OCD-level attention to detail and obsession with ensuring the product is ready to go before putting customers inside Anduril’s immersive wargaming and VR/AR world. Eligible to obtain and maintain associated country background check and security clearance to support increasingly complex and potentially classified exercises. Willingness to travel, be based in the UAE, and participate in collaboration with teammates in the UK and USA. Preferred Qualifications Experience with software engineering, especially hands on experience using & trouble shooting AR/VR technologies, virtual servers, audio/visual, and desktop software. Experience and familiarity with military operations, tactics, techniques, procedures, and hierarchies. Familiarity with Confluence, Jira, Slack, Quip, MS Office and Zoom as means to organize data and communicate across our teams effectively. Experience with military technology to include but not limited to: Unmanned systems (air and ground), Communications and Electronic Warfare equipment, Joint Fires and Maneuver Warfare munitions and vehicles to allow you to integrate more quickly and effectively within and across the Maneuver Dominance team and alongside the customer. Experience building trust with clients and teammates quickly and effectively under sometimes stressful conditions. Prior military or government leadership experience Benefits The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits. Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information. To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com. Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links. What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts. Together, we drive the shift to smart, efficient, and more sustainable mining. Make your impact You’ll play a key role in solving real-world challenges. Culture Change: Drive and embed a multi-strand strategic culture change through the Zero Harm Behaviour Framework, communicating effectively at all organisational levels from executives to shop floor. Risk and Compliance Management: Provide risk-based strategic and tactical support to the Senior regional team, Regional and General Managers, and employees; ensure SHE and legal compliance across all sites. Performance Monitoring: Report on SHE KPIs, identify trends, celebrate successes, and address areas needing improvement to maintain high safety standards. Hazard Control: Ensure rigorous risk assessment and accident management systems are in place to identify hazards and implement appropriate control measures. Regional Support and Travel: Visit and support sites across Southern Europe and North Africa, with a minimum of 6-7 trips per year including regular travel between Madrid and Seville. Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate closely with site managers and senior management, including sub-regional MDs and sales directors, to maintain strong reporting and operational support. Safety First: Demonstrate 100% commitment to our zero harm behaviours in support of our drive towards developing a world-class safety culture. What you’ll bring Must-haves: Formal qualification in SHE management (bachelor’s degree preferred) or equivalent education and experience. Proven experience managing SHE across multiple sites in a regional capacity. Strong communication skills with the ability to influence and engage senior management and diverse teams. Passionate about building and maintaining an engaging, safety-first culture with high ethical standards. Nice-to-haves: Certification such as NEBOSH or equivalent safety qualifications relevant to different countries. Background in psychology or wellbeing programmes, including mental health first aider certification. Experience in industries such as automotive, manufacturing, hospitality, or mining. We live our values we think safety first, do the right thing, respect each other, aim high, and delight our customers. We encourage our people to lead by example and celebrate our successes. We’re passionate about our purpose to help deliver the natural resources that are essential to create a better future for the world. We do this by combining our deep customer insights, world-class engineering, materials science expertise, and intelligent automation to deliver innovative end-to-end solutions incorporating our signature technologies. We believe your voice matters and your ideas make a difference. We’re working hard to nurture a diverse culture where our people feel like they belong and can do the best work of their lives. You can help shape our unique culture through our inclusion networks and safety initiatives. Benefits Competitive pay Career development and learning support Access to global inclusion networks Regional and team-specific benefits Sharebuilder scheme Wellness support for you and your family Collaboration with global teams Study support

This role leads the regional quality objectives to ensure right-first-time execution, customer satisfaction, compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements, and continuous reduction of Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ). The leader partners closely with Regional Operations, Project Management, Engineering, Sourcing, Manufacturing, Integration Facility teams, Services, and Commercial teams to prevent defects, strengthen quality culture, and drive Lean operational excellence through standard work, visual management, PSR, Kaizen, and continuous improvement. Job Description Key Responsibilities Strategic Leadership Define and deploy the regional quality strategy for Grid Automation MENAT in alignment with global business quality priorities, the Zero Defect framework, and Lean operating principles. Lead transformation initiatives to improve process capability, execution discipline, product and project quality, and customer outcomes across the region. Establish and drive regional quality goals, KPIs, and operating rhythms focused on prevention, flow, waste reduction, execution excellence, and continuous improvement. Ensure strong quality governance across projects, services, Integration Facilities, and regional operations, with clear accountability, tiered escalation, and disciplined follow-through. Promote a culture of Lean thinking by embedding standardization, visual management, daily management, Kaizen, and PSR into regional quality processes. Drive simplification and harmonization of quality processes across MENAT to reduce variation, improve responsiveness, and increase process maturity. Project & Operational Quality Own quality performance across the regional project and service execution lifecycle. Ensure effective deployment of quality controls, quality gates, control plans, risk reviews, and lessons learned throughout project execution. Lead robust management of non-conformances, PSR, root cause analysis, and corrective/preventive actions to ensure timely closure and sustainable improvements. Improve process flow and execution consistency by standardizing key quality deliverables, handoff points, and escalation practices across the region. Integration Facilities Quality Initiatives Lead the quality strategy and improvement roadmap for regional Integration Facilities, ensuring robust process control, standardization, and right-first-time panel, cubicle, and system integration. Drive preventive quality initiatives across Integration Facilities to reduce wiring defects, configuration errors, missing documentation, testing escapes, rework, and late-stage nonconformances. Improve traceability, defect capture, and feedback loops between Engineering, Sourcing, Integration Facilities, and Project teams to ensure recurring issues are addressed at the root cause. Lead Kaizen initiatives within Integration Facilities to improve workstation discipline, material flow, standard work adherence, visual management, and first-pass yield. Drive PSR and root cause rigor for major defects and repeat issues originating in Integration Facilities, ensuring sustainable corrective and preventive actions. Customer Quality & Stakeholder Engagement Serve as the regional quality leader for critical customer issues and escalations, ensuring strong ownership, transparent communication, and timely resolution. Partner with commercial, project, and service teams to strengthen customer confidence and improve customer quality experience across the MENAT region. Lead customer issue resolution processes with strong discipline around containment, PSR, root cause analysis, corrective actions, verification of effectiveness, and prevention of recurrence.
